Regarding the email, the original tone is aggressive, personal, and unprofessional, which can damage employee morale and create legal risks. A better approach is to be firm about the deadline, objective about the pattern of behavior, and focused on solutions and expectations rather than threats to employment.

Here is a revised version of the email:

Subject: Follow-up on Project Submission Deadline

Hi [Employee Name],

I noticed that the project submission was not received by the deadline. This is the second time this has happened recently, and it is impacting our team’s workflow.

Please let me know if there were any obstacles preventing you from meeting the deadline. Going forward, I need to see consistent adherence to our submission schedules. If you are facing challenges that might affect your ability to meet deadlines, please let me know so we can discuss how to support you.

Let’s connect briefly tomorrow to ensure we are aligned on upcoming deliverables.

Best regards,

[Your Name]
